title: Landing page copy draft — Regulated workloads (Dedicated + Private)
body:
Doc: Regulated workloads landing page copy (draft)
Owner: Ethan Wallace
Primary reviewers: Soojin Lee (PMM), Naomi Feldman (Security/Compliance), Elliot Price (Docs)
Last working session: 2025-05-16
Target audience: Security/IT + platform/ML engineering buyers in regulated environments (finserv + healthcare PHI-adjacent) evaluating Dedicated capacity or Private (VPC/on-prem).

=== Page goals (internal) ===
1) Convert regulated-intent traffic into security + architecture review calls.
2) Pre-answer the top security objections without over-claiming.
3) Create a clean “path” for evidence: Security FAQ + Evidence Pack Index + request flow.

[PMM NOTE — Soojin, 5/04]
Keep this page outcome-focused. Don’t lead with “we have SOC2” — lead with predictable serving + controls/security posture. Put compliance artifacts behind CTA and NDA language.

[SECURITY REVIEW — Naomi, 5/05]
Avoid “HIPAA-ready”, “PCI compliant”, “guaranteed compliance”, “certified” unless we can substantiate. Use: “supports deployments and controls commonly required for…” and “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA”. Any HIPAA references must include BAA language + scope caveat.


============================================================
SECTION 1 — HERO (headline options + subhead + primary CTA)
============================================================
Headline options (choose 1):
A) Run LLM inference for regulated workloads—without trading off performance.
B) High-performance LLM inference with the controls regulated teams require.
C) Dedicated and Private LLM inference for security- and compliance-driven teams.
D) Predictable LLM serving for financial services and healthcare teams.

Subhead options:
1) Deploy Redwood in dedicated capacity or private environments (VPC/on-prem), with auditability, identity controls, configurable retention, and customer-managed key options—plus the latency and throughput you need for production.
2) Redwood Inference helps teams ship LLM features with predictable performance and the security posture required for regulated environments: deployment isolation, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and encryption controls.

Primary CTA (recommended): Book a security + architecture review
Secondary CTA: Request the evidence pack (NDA) / View security FAQ

Hero supporting bullets (3–4 max):
- Dedicated capacity or Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)
- Audit logs and access controls (RBAC; SSO/SAML options)
- Encryption in transit and at rest; customer-managed keys supported in Private deployments
- Predictable throughput and rollout controls (pin versions, canary, fallback)

Form microcopy (if we gate CTA):
- “Tell us what you’re deploying (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and your compliance constraints. We’ll respond within 1 business day.”

[PMM NOTE]
If we offer two CTAs, keep “Book review” primary. Evidence pack request should route to Security ops (Olga/Daniel) with qualification.


============================================================
SECTION 2 — WHO THIS IS FOR (quick ICP callout)
============================================================
Suggested header: Built for teams operating under strict security, privacy, and audit requirements

Copy:
Whether you’re modernizing customer support, automating document workflows, or scaling internal assistants, Redwood helps you run LLM inference with the deployment isolation, observability, and governance controls that regulated environments demand.

Use-case examples (keep generic + safe):
- Financial services: customer communications, policy QA, risk and compliance research assistance, operations automation
- Healthcare (PHI-adjacent): member support, clinical/claims summarization, coding assistance, internal knowledge assistants

[SECURITY REVIEW]
Avoid stating we “process PHI” as a blanket statement. Use “PHI-adjacent” and “subject to customer configuration and contractual terms.”


============================================================
SECTION 3 — DEPLOYMENT OPTIONS (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — focus on Dedicated/Private
============================================================
Header: Choose the deployment model that matches your risk posture

Intro:
Redwood provides a consistent inference API and operational tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For regulated workloads, most teams choose Dedicated or Private for stronger isolation and more control.

Cards:
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation
- Configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options
- SLA-backed uptime and support tiers (details in contracting)
CTA: “Talk to an expert about Dedicated”

2) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Private control plane with customer-managed networking
- VPC deployment options; on-prem packages for restricted environments
- Customer-managed keys supported (KMS/HSM integrations depending on environment)
CTA: “Review a Private reference architecture”

3) Redwood Hosted API (when appropriate)
- Fastest path to production for less restrictive workloads
- Same model catalog and runtime optimizations
CTA: “See API docs”

[PMM NOTE]
Don’t bury Hosted, but don’t lead with it. We want regulated buyers to self-select into Dedicated/Private without feeling like Hosted is “non-secure.”


============================================================
SECTION 4 — SECURITY & GOVERNANCE (core claims + proof language)
============================================================
Header: Security controls for regulated environments (without slowing teams down)

Bullets (approved-style language):
- Auditability: audit logs to support investigations, compliance reporting, and access review workflows
- Identity and access: role-based access control (RBAC); SSO/SAML options available for enterprise deployments
- Encryption: TLS in transit and encryption at rest; customer-managed keys supported for Private deployments
- Data controls: configurable data retention options by deployment; logging controls to help reduce sensitive data exposure
- Network isolation: VPC and on-prem deployment patterns for restricted network environments
- Operational governance: model version pinning, controlled rollouts, and fallback policies to support safe change management

Proof / “how to validate” callout:
Want to evaluate fit quickly? We can run a 30–45 minute security + architecture review and share an evidence pack under NDA.

Buttons:
- Primary: Book a security + architecture review
- Secondary: Request evidence pack (NDA)

[SECURITY REVIEW — Naomi]
Replace “SAML/SCIM” with “SSO/SAML options” unless we’re prepared to answer SCIM specifics on the page. Keep SCIM discussion in FAQ or in sales/security calls.


============================================================
SECTION 5 — PERFORMANCE + ECONOMICS (tie to regulated buyer priorities)
============================================================
Header: Predictable latency and cost—so compliance doesn’t become a tax

Copy:
Regulated teams often need more than a model endpoint—they need predictable serving behavior, visibility into performance and spend, and safe rollout controls. Redwood’s runtime and Console are built to make inference measurable and operable in production.

Bullets:
- Token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Redwood Console
- Workload-aware batching/caching recommendations to reduce unit cost
- Routing and fallback policies to maintain reliability during spikes
- Rollouts (canary/A-B) to reduce risk during model or config changes

[PMM NOTE]
Keep this section short and concrete. We can link to a benchmark download later (optional) but don’t make it the primary CTA.


============================================================
SECTION 6 — “WHAT YOU’LL GET” (evaluation offer / pilot plan)
============================================================
Header: A clear path from first call to production

Option A (simple):
1) Security + architecture review (30–45 min)
2) Evidence pack under NDA + Q&A
3) Optional technical pilot (1–2 weeks): benchmark + architecture validation
4) Procurement-ready package: deployment scope, support tier, and rollout plan

Option B (more technical):
- Reference architecture review (Dedicated vs Private)
- Success criteria defined upfront (latency/throughput, logging, retention, identity)
- Joint test plan + integration checkpoints

CTA: “Book a review”

[SECURITY REVIEW]
Avoid promising “procurement-ready” timelines. Use “procurement support” and “we can provide standard artifacts under NDA.”


============================================================
SECTION 7 — FAQ (on-page mini FAQ; link to full security FAQ)
============================================================
Header: Common questions from regulated teams

Q: Do you have a SOC 2 report?
A: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report that can be shared under NDA as part of our evidence pack.

Q: Can Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports private deployments (VPC and on-prem options). We’ll align on networking, key management, logging, and operational requirements during the architecture review.

Q: What audit logging is available?
A: Redwood provides audit logs to support access review and operational investigations. We can share sample fields/export patterns during a technical deep dive.

Q: What are the data retention options?
A: Retention and logging controls vary by deployment model and contract. We’ll document requirements and map them to the recommended deployment during the review.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A: Private deployments can support customer-managed keys (e.g., via KMS/HSM depending on environment). We’ll review key management requirements and operational responsibilities in the reference architecture.

Footer link: “Read the full security FAQ”

[PMM NOTE]
Avoid super-specific guarantees (e.g., “90-day retention by default”) on the landing page. Keep specifics in the FAQ + evidence pack.


============================================================
SECTION 8 — FINAL CTA (bottom-of-page)
============================================================
Header options:
- Ready to evaluate Redwood for a regulated workload?
- Get a security + architecture review this week

Primary CTA: Book a security + architecture review
Secondary CTA: Request evidence pack (NDA)

CTA helper text:
We’ll help you choose the right deployment (Dedicated vs Private), map security requirements to controls, and outline a pilot plan if needed.


============================================================
SECURITY FOOTNOTES / LEGAL-SAFE LANGUAGE (draft)
============================================================
Footnote block (small text at bottom):
1) “Evidence pack materials (including audit samples and compliance reports) are shared under NDA and subject to confidentiality restrictions.”
2) “Security controls and deployment options may vary by product tier and deployment model (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Final commitments are defined in the applicable order form and agreements.”
3) “References to regulated frameworks (e.g., HIPAA, PCI, GDPR) describe common customer requirements and do not constitute a certification or guarantee of compliance. Customers are responsible for their own compliance programs and configurations.”
4) “Where applicable, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are supported for Private deployments; integration specifics depend on the customer environment and chosen deployment architecture.”

[SECURITY REVIEW — Dr. Rahman]
Footnote #3 is critical. Also avoid “HIPAA” in top-level headlines. If we mention it, do so in FAQ with BAA language.


============================================================
OPEN QUESTIONS (internal)
============================================================
1) Terminology: “SSO/SAML” vs “SAML/SCIM” — keep SCIM off the landing page?
2) Evidence pack request workflow: route to Olga/Daniel? Add qualification fields (company, vertical, deployment interest).
3) Should we include a “download architecture diagram” asset or keep all CTAs meeting-based for ABM?
4) Do we want a dedicated block for “data residency” or keep it in retention/data controls?


============================================================
CHANGELOG (high level)
============================================================
- 2025-05-04: Soojin tightened hero + reduced compliance-first framing.
- 2025-05-05: Naomi flagged disallowed language (“HIPAA-ready”, “certified”) and added footnote guidance.
- 2025-05-16: Added deployment section + simplified FAQ; aligned CTAs to security + architecture review.
